editorial.material: White begins a pawn behind. The rook sacrifice takes the g7 pawn; the king then captures the f6 rook, gaining one pawn overall.
editorial.motif: The g7 pawn defends the rook on f6, so the white king cannot capture it at the start. Rxg7+ removes the pawn; if Kxg7, Re7+ moves the king away and Kxf6 captures the rook. Re6 interposes against Rd6+ and the rook on e6 is protected by the king.
editorial.alternatives: All starting moves were searched at 100000 nodes; the immediate replies after Rxg7+ and Re7+ at 80000 nodes and all 15 replies after Kxf6 at 100000 nodes. No immediate mate or forced mate in two solver moves found. ...Kf8 and ...Kh8 to the first check allow Kxf6 while the rook on g7 survives. The original game used ...Kg8 and ...a4, which is preserved as a separate line. Engine searches are bounded.

editorial.material: Equal material initially. The published line gains the f7, g6 and h6 pawns while Black recovers a5, leaving a net gain of two pawns.
editorial.motif: The bishop d5 protects f7. Nxd5 Rxd5 exchanges the bishop and leaves f7 unguarded, allowing Rxf7+. Direct Rxf7+ Bxf7 loses the rook. After ...Kg8 the rook moves to f6 and later recovers pawns despite ...Rxa5.
editorial.alternatives: All starting moves probed at 100000 nodes; the 19 replies to Nxd5 and two replies to Rxf7+ at 80000 nodes, plus all 23 replies after Rf6 at 80000 nodes. No immediate mate or forced mate in two solver moves found. The principal line was played; ...g5 and ...Kh8 alternatives are analysis. Searches are bounded, not exhaustive proof.

editorial.material: Black starts one pawn ahead and wins another pawn after an equal knight-for-bishop exchange.
editorial.motif: The white bishop e3 protects the pawn f4. Nxe3 Qxe3 exchanges the defender and Bxf4 takes the pawn while attacking the queen. Direct Bxf4 Bxf4 exchanges bishops without a gain. If Qf2 attacks the black queen h4, ...Qh6 saves it.
editorial.method: All legal starting moves searched at 100000 nodes; all 32 replies to Nxe3 and all 40 replies to Bxf4 searched at 80000 nodes. No immediate mate or mate in two solver moves found. The principal line was played; Qf2 is an analysis alternative. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: White starts a pawn ahead; after the pawn exchange the rook takes f5, Black takes a3 and White recovers a4, retaining a net pawn gain.
editorial.motif: The pawn g6 protects f5. hxg6 Kxg6 exchanges it, allowing Rxf5. Direct Rxf5 gxf5 Kxf5 loses a rook for two pawns. The king or rook then responds to the counterattack on a3.
editorial.alternatives: All legal initial moves were probed at 100000 nodes, the 19 replies after hxg6 and 15 after Rxf5 at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. The principal line through ...Kf7 was played, while the final Rxa4 and the Kxe4 branch are analysis. Searches are bounded.

beginner-01-review.concept: Bxd3+ exchanges the defending bishop; after Kxd3, Rxb1 wins the rook. If the king moves instead, Bxb1 wins it.

beginner-02-review.concept: Rxd5+ removes the rook defending d4. The pawn recapture allows Nxd4; otherwise Rxd4 wins the bishop.

beginner-03-review.concept: Ra7+ checks and diverts the king guarding the bishop; after either legal king move Rxa4 captures the bishop. Direct Bxa4 Kxa4 exchanges bishops without gain. The checking rook is attacked after Kb6 but escapes by capturing on a4.

beginner-04-review.concept: Rxh6+ exchanges the rooks and diverts the king from guarding g4; Bxg4 wins the bishop. The bishop-check alternatives divert the same king from h6.

beginner-05-review.concept: cxd5+ removes the knight guarding f6; the king must answer the check. Bxf6 then wins the bishop. Direct Bxf6 Nxf6 is an equal trade.

editorial.material: White starts one pawn behind. In the game line, White wins the bishop on e7 and recovers the g5 pawn while Black takes c3: a net gain of three points from the start, leaving White two points ahead. Bf4+ and Be5 preserve the attacked bishop.
editorial.motif: The queen f6 protects bishop e7, so immediate Rxe7 loses the rook to Qxe7. After fxg5 hxg5, Rf1 attacks the queen; moving it away leaves e7 available. The threat to the queen is the decision that removes the defender.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starting moves were searched at 100000 nodes and all immediate replies at each step of the collector sample at 80000. The game branch after Qxc3 Rxe7 and after Bxg5 received all-reply 80000-node probes. After Qxg5 Bxg5 Bxg5 Rxf7, the queen is exchanged for bishop and pawn; after Qg6, the rook exchange leads to Bxc5. Rxe7, Bxc5, Rb7+ and Rxa7 initially fail. These engine screens are not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: B: the direct pawn exchange prepares a rook attack on the defending queen; the payoff Rxe7 is reached on the third solver move without sacrifice. Later moves demonstrate material recovery and safety rather than artificially elevating the level.

editorial.material: Equal material initially. The rooks exchange and Bxf4 wins a pawn while attacking the remaining white rook; Re2 or Re1 saves it.
editorial.motif: The white rook f2 guards f4. Rxf2 Kxf2 removes it; immediate Bxf4 Rxf4 loses the bishop.
editorial.alternatives: All starting moves and the immediate replies after Rxf2 and Bxf4 were searched at 100000 and 80000 nodes. The actual game continuation and the Re1 alternative both preserve the pawn gain. Other replies to Rxf2 include Rg3+ Kh8 followed by the exchange. These searches are bounded, not exhaustive proof.
editorial.classification: A: a direct rook exchange and bishop capture with a clear tempo, no sacrifice.

editorial.material: White is one pawn ahead initially; the principal line wins a knight after an equal minor-piece exchange.
editorial.motif: The bishop f5 guards the black knight on h3, making Kxh3 illegal. Nxf5 removes that bishop and after ...Rxf5 the king can capture the knight. After ...Qxf5 instead, Rxd5 Qxd5 Qe8+ Kh7 Kxh3 recovers the material and wins the knight.
editorial.method: All legal initial moves probed at 100000 nodes; every immediate reply after Nxf5 and Kxh3 probed at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves was found. The sample until ...Qf6 was played; the subsequent queen maneuvers and alternative are analysis. Bounded searches are not exhaustive proof.

headers.TimeControl: Standard: 90 minutes with 30 second increment from move 1
headers.WhiteTeam: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley-A

editorial.material: Material starts equal. The main line exchanges bishop for knight, sacrifices another bishop for a pawn, wins the queen, and allows a rook to capture a knight: a net gain of four points.
editorial.motif: The d4 knight and g2 king both protect the queen f3. Bxd4 removes the knight. After Bxd4, the checking bishop sacrifice Bxh3+ draws the king away; Qxf3 then wins the queen. Immediate Bxh3+ fails to win the queen because the knight can recapture on f3, while immediate Qxf3 after the exchange allows Kxf3.
editorial.alternatives: All legal roots and all immediate replies after the first three solver moves were screened at 100000 and 80000 nodes. The four replies to Bxh3+ include Kxh3 and Kh2; the saved line continues through the rook capture. Moving or exchanging the queen after Bxd4 allows Black to keep the knight gain. Engine probes are bounded and are not exhaustive proof.
editorial.classification: C: a bishop is deliberately given for a pawn with check to divert the king and win the queen.

editorial.material: Material starts equal. Black exchanges a bishop for a knight, wins the b3 pawn and then exchanges a knight for the rook on a1, gaining three points.
editorial.motif: The white knight d2 and queen c2 both defend b3. Bxd2 Qxd2 exchanges the knight and moves the queen off c2. Nxb3 then attacks the queen and rook; after the queen moves, Nxa1 Rxa1 completes the material gain. Direct Nxb3 Qxb3 loses the knight for a pawn.
editorial.method: All starting moves searched at 100000 nodes; all 34 replies to Bxd2 and all 40 replies after Nxb3 searched at 80000 nodes. No immediate mate or mate in two solver moves found. The principal line is played; ...Qh6 is analysis. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: Black begins one pawn behind; the sacrifice and recovery gain three points from the start, leaving Black two points ahead. The line continues through the check on the black king, who can escape.
editorial.motif: The white knight f1 guards rook d2. Rh1+ sacrifices the rook to draw the white king off g1; Qxf1+ removes the knight. Qf4+ reaches a diagonal from which Qxd2 captures the rook. Without the sacrifice, Qxd2 Nxd2 and Qxf1+ Kxf1 fail.
editorial.alternatives: All legal initial moves were searched at 100000 nodes and all immediate white replies at the four forcing solver moves at 80000 nodes. Rh1+ and Qxf1+ each have only one legal king response; Qf4+ has four. The three king escapes after Qh3+ were separately searched at 500000 nodes each. These bounded searches do not constitute exhaustive proof. The main line is the game continuation.
editorial.classification: D: rook sacrifice followed by queen checks, removal of the knight, and recovery of the rook; five solver moves shown including king safety.

firouzja-vachier-review.editorial: The c1 bishop is the sole defender of b2; Nxc1 removes it, and after Rxc1 Bxb2 wins a pawn. Direct Bxb2 Bxb2 loses a bishop for a pawn. All legal roots and replies to both solver moves were probed; engine scores remain bounded evidence. Black starts one pawn ahead.

editorial.material: Equal at the start; a bishop is sacrificed for the f7 pawn, followed by a queen exchange and a rook capture of the c7 knight, leaving a net pawn gain.
editorial.motif: The queen d7 defends the knight c7. The bishop sacrifice with check induces Qxf7, after which Qxf7+ removes the defending queen. The rook on c1 captures the newly undefended knight. If the king declines the bishop sacrifice, the bishop can retreat while retaining the pawn.
editorial.alternatives: All starting moves were independently searched at 100000 nodes, with no immediate mate or forced mate in two solver moves found. All 3 replies to Bxf7+ and both replies to Qxf7+ were searched at 80000 nodes. d5 Ncxd5 does not produce the displayed gain. ...Qxf7 is the played line; king moves are analysis. These bounded searches are not exhaustive proof.

gharibyan-deac-review.editorial: Black is three pawns down initially. Nxc3+ removes the bishop defending e1; both Kc2 and Rxc3 permit Rxe1, yielding a rook after the knight is recovered. Direct Rxe1+ Bxe1 is an equal exchange. The material gain does not depend on the game result.

editorial.material: White starts one pawn behind; the shown exchanges gain two points, leaving White a pawn ahead.
editorial.motif: The rook on f8 defends the bishop on c8. Rxf8 exchanges the defender; after Kxf8 the knight can take the bishop. Direct Nxc8 permits Nxf2, attacking the rook. In the teaching continuation Kf2 defends g2 and attacks the black knight.
editorial.method: All legal initial moves probed at 100000 nodes; every immediate reply along the screened sample probed at 80000 nodes. Mate in one and in two solver moves checked separately. Bounded analysis is not exhaustive game-tree proof.

editorial.material: Equal material at the start. Black sacrifices a rook for the knight f3 and then captures the bishop d2, gaining one pawn by material value.
editorial.motif: The knight f3 guards the bishop d2. Qd8 places the queen behind the d3 rook; after Rxf3 Qxf3 the rook has vacated the d-file and the queen captures d2. Direct Rxd2 Nxd2 loses the rook for a bishop.
editorial.method: All legal starting moves searched at 100000 nodes. All 30 replies after Qd8, 25 replies after Rxf3, and 25 replies after Qxd2 were searched at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. Qd8 is an analysis preparation; the original game began Rfd8 and is preserved separately. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: Equal material initially. Rook for bishop followed by the knight wins one point; Bb3 escapes the pawn attack.
editorial.motif: The bishop on e6 guards c4; Rxe6 removes it. The direct Bxc4 Bxc4 is an equal exchange.
editorial.alternatives: All legal roots and all immediate replies at the collector sample were searched at 100000 and 80000 nodes respectively; fxe6 and Rxe6 both allow Bxc4. After Re4, Bd3 attacks the rook and tactically protects the other bishop. Other defensively relevant moves were screened; these are bounded searches, not exhaustive proof.
editorial.classification: A, direct capture and recovery, no sacrifice.

editorial.material: Material begins equal. The queens are exchanged; the knight manoeuvres, avoids capture by d6 and the bishop takes c6, leaving White a pawn ahead. The white rook f1 protects the bishop f2 from the rook on e2.
editorial.motif: The black queen c3 and bishop d7 both defend c6. Qxc3 Bxc3 removes the queen, Ne4 drives the recapturing bishop back and Nc5 attacks the remaining bishop. After Bf5, Na6 saves the knight from dxc5 before Bxc6 wins the pawn.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starting moves were searched at 150000 nodes and all immediate replies at each solver stage of the actual game line at 100000 nodes. Direct Bxc6 Bxc6 loses a bishop for the pawn. Taking c6 immediately after Nc5 Bf5 permits dxc5, and the remaining sequence does not establish a durable gain. If Black plays dxc5 immediately after Nc5, Rxd7 and Rxc7 replace the lost knight with bishop and pawn. Re2 attacks the f2 bishop, protected by the f1 rook. Searches are bounded and not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: C*: five solver moves without sacrifice; the knight must attack a second defender and escape the d6 pawn before the capture. The game continuation is shown.

editorial.material: Black begins one pawn behind. The knight/bishop and queen exchanges are equal, then Nxc2 wins a knight. The f4 pawn sequence shows material recovery and adds a pawn; the Black advantage is at least two points overall.
editorial.motif: The bishop b3 defends the knight c2 from the queen b2. Nxb3 exchanges the bishop. On Qxb3, the intermezzo Ne1+ places the other knight to capture c2 after Qxb3 axb3. Immediate Qxc2+ loses the queen to Bxc2.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starting moves were screened at 100000 nodes and every immediate reply on the original candidate line at 80000. After axb3 Black has Qxc2+; after Qxd3, Nd4 and Nxc2 recover the second knight. The f4 pawn captures are shown through gxf4. The game ended immediately after Nxb3, so subsequent moves are analysis. Engine searches are bounded and not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: C*: no sacrifice; a knight check between exchanges is needed to reach c2 after the queen trade, and the continuation resolves the f4 pawn counterplay.

editorial.material: White starts two pawns behind by material value. The rook sacrifice captures a bishop; after the rook recapture the white bishop takes a knight, a net material gain of one pawn.
editorial.motif: The bishop e6 defends the knight d5. Rxe6 sacrifices a rook to remove that bishop, so after ...Rxe6 the bishop on b3 can capture d5. Direct Bxd5 Bxd5 loses the bishop for the knight.
editorial.method: All legal initial moves independently searched at 100000 nodes; all 45 immediate replies to Rxe6 and all 34 replies after Bxd5 searched at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. The main line was played; ...Bh2+ is analysis. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: Equal initially. The knight exchange and Bxd5 win a pawn.
editorial.motif: The f6 knight protects the d5 pawn. Nxf6+ exchanges that defender, allowing Bxd5; direct Bxd5 Nxd5 loses the bishop. ...Qxf6 gives a different continuation, and ...Ne7 attacks the bishop, which can capture the b7 bishop.
editorial.method: All starting moves searched at 100000 nodes; all five immediate replies to Nxf6+ and all 33 replies after Bxd5 searched at 80000 nodes. No immediate mate or forced mate in two solver moves found. The main line through ...Rc8 was played; the subsequent queen retreat and the two extra branches are analysis. Engine searches are bounded.

kvaloy-campos-review.editorial: Exchange sacrifice of rook for knight, with two checking moves and a counter-exchange before the bishop can collect the target; five solver moves. Nxd1 Bf3+ Kxf3 gxf6 is a second relevant defence. A direct Bxe4 Nxe4 is an equal exchange.

editorial.material: White starts one pawn ahead and gains another pawn in the displayed continuation.
editorial.motif: The black knight on f5 protects g7. The knight from g3 exchanges it by Nxf5 Rxf5, and the knight on e6 can then take g7. Direct Nxg7 Nxg7 loses the knight. After ...Re5 the queen on e3 is attacked and moves to d2.
editorial.method: Every legal starting move was probed at 100000 nodes and every immediate reply to Nxf5 and Nxg7 at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. The saved variation through Bf3 was played in the game. These engine searches are bounded, not exhaustive proof.

macias-almagro-review.editorial: Exchange the bishop defending g7, then take the pawn with the other knight. The displayed ...Nb4 a3 addresses a pawn fork. The original game instead used ...Rxf8 and ...f4. Direct Nxg7 Bxg7 loses the knight for the pawn.

editorial.material: Equal at the start. The played line wins the black queen, knight and two pawns for two rooks, and the continuation saves the knight attacked by ...f5.
editorial.motif: The first rook clears b6; the second rook exchanges itself for the queen on b7. The queen guarded the knight on a6, which can then be captured.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starting moves received 100000-node Stockfish searches; no mate in one or two solver moves was found. Qxb7+ Kxb7 Nxf6 Rxd6 exchanges queens and pawns without a material gain. The 80000-node reply screens cover every legal reply at each sample position, not a mathematical exhaustive proof. Qxb6 and axb6 are principal capture defences.
editorial.classification: The initial rook is sacrificed, followed by coordination of the second rook and queen; the sample contains more than three solver moves.

editorial.material: White begins one pawn ahead. The main line exchanges bishop for knight, wins the pawn f6, and then exchanges queens and the remaining bishops, leaving White two pawns ahead.
editorial.motif: The black knight e8 guards f6. Bxe8 removes it; after either Rxe8 or Qxe8, Qxf6 wins the pawn. Direct Qxf6 is met by Nxf6.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starting moves and all immediate replies at the sample stages were searched at 100000 and 80000 nodes. Both rook and queen recaptures are saved through the queen exchanges. If Black takes the attacked queen by Bxh6, Bxd7 wins the black queen. These searches are bounded, not exhaustive proofs. The game ended after Qxf6; the subsequent moves are analysis.
editorial.classification: A: directly exchange the knight guarding the pawn, then handle an ordinary queen exchange.

editorial.material: Black starts two pawns behind by material value; the complete line gains a minor piece (three points), leaving Black a pawn ahead.
editorial.motif: The bishop on f3 protects the knight on e4. Rxf3 Rxf3 exchanges it for a rook; Bxe4 captures the knight and simultaneously attacks the rook on f3. After Kg2 Bxf3+ Kxf3, Black has gained the two white minor pieces for a rook and bishop. Direct Bxe4 Bxe4 exchanges bishops and fails to obtain the knight for free.
editorial.method: All legal initial moves searched at 100000 nodes; every immediate reply after Rxf3 and Bxe4 probed at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. The early moves through Kg2 were played; the direct Bxf3+ recapture is an illustrative analysis line, and the resulting endgame was checked at 500000 nodes. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: White begins one pawn ahead and gains another pawn after equal knight and rook exchanges.
editorial.motif: The bishop f6 guards the pawn e5. Nxf6 Rxf6 exchanges that defender, and Qxe5 wins the pawn. If Black responds ...Rxd6, Qxd6 recaptures the rook. Direct Qxe5 Bxe5 loses the queen.
editorial.alternatives: The game continued Rd8+, but it is unnecessary for the material objective: the shorter Qxe5 and ...Rxd6 Qxd6 achieve it. The exercise is therefore B, not C*. All initial moves were searched at 100000 nodes; all 27 replies after Nxf6 and all 29 after the shorter Qxe5 were searched at 80000 and 150000 nodes respectively. The short line and ...e4 line are analysis; the original game is preserved separately. Searches are bounded.

editorial.material: Black starts one pawn ahead and gains another pawn with the displayed line.
editorial.motif: The white pawn on e4 and knight on c3 both defend d5. fxe4+ captures the pawn with check, and Nxe4 diverts the knight, leaving d5 unguarded. After Rxd5+ the king protects g7 to prevent a material countercapture. Direct Rxd5+ Nxd5 loses the rook.
editorial.method: All legal initial moves probed at 100000 nodes; every immediate reply along the screened sample probed at 80000 nodes. Mate in one and in two solver moves checked separately. Bounded analysis is not exhaustive game-tree proof.

petrov-gurel-review.editorial: The c4 rook is the only defender of c5. Rxc4 exchanges it, allowing Qxc5; White can recapture with queen, knight or pawn. Direct Rxc5 Rxc5 Qxc5 Qxc5 loses the black queen. All legal roots and replies were probed; bounded scores do not prove every later continuation.

piorun-niemann-review.editorial: The rook on f2 defends f6. Rxf2+ exchanges rooks, then Qxf6 captures the pawn; both Kxf2 and Qxf2 were checked. Direct gxf6 allows White Qa7+ and counterplay; the short engine review does not show a comparable simple gain. Scores are bounded evidence.

editorial.material: Material starts equal. In the game line, bishop and knight are exchanged and White wins the e4 pawn. Retreating the bishop or taking d4 leads to the saved exchange-winning alternatives.
editorial.motif: The bishop on d5 protects the pawn e4. Nc3 attacks that bishop; after Nf6 Nxd5 Nxd5, Bxe4 wins the pawn. Direct Bxe4 is answered Bxe4, losing the bishop for a pawn.
editorial.alternatives: All legal roots and immediate black replies after each solver move in the sample were screened at 100000 and 80000 nodes. After Bb3, the rook-check resource Rg6+ is met by Bxg6 hxg6; after cxd4, Nxd5 Rxc1 Rxc1 resolves the rook capture. The alternative initial dxc5 allows Nxc5 and does not immediately gain material. Searches are bounded and not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: B: a quiet knight attack prepares a short exchange of the defender, with no sacrifice.

sharifov-sebenik-review.editorial: The knight e5 is the sole defender of c6. The bishop exchanges it, after which the rook captures c6. Direct Rxc6 Nxc6 loses the rook for a pawn. After b5 Ra6, bxa4 bxa4 restores the pawn gain; other defences are bounded engine evidence.

headers.TimeControl: Standard: 90 minutes with 30 second increment from move 1
headers.BlackTeam: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley-B

editorial.material: Material begins equal. After the queen exchange, Black gives a rook for a bishop and takes a knight, a net gain of one point. Nxd4 gains another pawn; the continuation includes the defensive check and king escape.
editorial.motif: The white bishop e2 guards knight f3. Rxe2 removes it by an exchange sacrifice; after Rxe2 Bxf3 the bishop h5 takes the knight. That knight in turn guarded d4, so the c6 knight can capture the d4 pawn.
editorial.alternatives: All legal roots and all immediate white replies on the extended game line were searched at 100000 and 80000 nodes. Rxe2 first is an equivalent motif-based move: both Qxf5 Rxf5 and Rxe2 Qxb1 preserve the exchange sacrifice and Bxf3. Direct Bxf3 permits Qxf5 Rxf5 and does not win the knight as shown. The actual game continuation includes Re8+ Kg7. These searches are bounded, not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: C: a rook is deliberately given for a bishop to remove the knight defender; the later checks show material recovery rather than a harder grade.

editorial.material: White starts one pawn ahead and gains another pawn after equal exchanges of two rooks.
editorial.motif: The rook e7 defends h7. Rxe7 Rxe7 Rxe7 Kxe7 exchanges it and the other pair of rooks, allowing Nxh7. A quiet Kc3 can also prepare the same motif when Black exchanges on e5: Kc3 Rxe5 fxe5+ Ke7 Nxh7.
editorial.method: All legal starting moves searched at 100000 nodes; all 15, nine and twelve immediate replies after the three solver moves of the screened line searched at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves was found. The principal line was played; the Kc3 variation is analysis. Searches are bounded, not exhaustive proof.

editorial.material: White exchanges two knights for a rook and two pawns, gaining one point; the e4 pawn survives on f5 in the main line. The displayed queen exchange leaves the material gain intact.
editorial.motif: Ncxe5 draws the e8 rook to e5. Nxe5 exchanges the rook guarding f5, after which ...Qxe5 replaces its defense. exf5 attacks the queen along the open e-file. If ...Qxf5, g4 attacks both queen and knight and the pawn takes h5; after ...gxh5 the material gain remains.
editorial.alternatives: All starting moves were searched at 100000 nodes, and the 35, 33 and 48 immediate replies after the first three solver moves at 80000 nodes. All 40 replies after the key g4 fork received 100000-node probes. The shorter direct exf5 permits ...bxc4, winning the knight. None of these searches is an exhaustive proof. The game used Na5 rather than this analysis line.
editorial.classification: A first knight is given for a pawn and a second is exchanged for the rook, followed by a pawn capture and a queen exchange; the four-solver-move combination and alternative fork require advanced coordination.

editorial.material: Material begins equal. After the bishop and knight exchange, Nxe4 wins a pawn. The played continuation wins g3 and saves the knight, and the rook escapes the attack from Bb6.
editorial.motif: The knight c3 protects e4. Bxc3+ exchanges the knight, and Nxe4 wins the pawn. If White recaptures with the queen, the queen exchange still allows Nxe4; Qxe4 first is another order exploiting the same removal.
editorial.alternatives: All legal starts and all immediate white replies in the candidate line were searched at 120000 and 80000 nodes. After Nxg3, hxg3 permits Rxh1+ because the h-file opens; the game used Rg1 Nf5 instead. The king and queen recaptures after Bxc3+ were reviewed, including Qxc3 Qxc3+ bxc3 Nxe4. Searches are bounded, not exhaustive proofs.
editorial.classification: B: a checking exchange removes the defender and a short tactical continuation handles the attempted knight capture.

editorial.material: Equal initially. After equal queen exchanges White wins the e5 pawn; the continuation moves the knight away from the attack by ...f6.
editorial.motif: The queen g5 defends the pawn e5. After Qxg5 hxg5, the c4 knight takes e5, and Ng4 preserves the knight after ...f6. Direct Nxe5 Qxe5 loses the knight.
editorial.alternatives: All legal initial moves probed at 100000 nodes; all immediate replies after Qxg5 and Nxe5 were searched at 80000 nodes. No mate in one or two solver moves found. The sample through ...Ke7 is the game; ...Rh6 is analysis. Searches are bounded, not exhaustive proof.

editorial.material: Equal material initially; the game continuation wins a pawn after equal bishop and queen exchanges.
editorial.motif: The bishop e7 defends d6. Bxe7 removes it; after Qxe7, Qxd6 obtains the pawn, and Rxd6 recaptures if Black exchanges queens. Direct Qxd6 Bxd6 Rxd6 loses queen for bishop and pawn.
editorial.method: All legal starting moves searched at 100000 nodes; every immediate reply after the screened solver moves was searched at 80000 nodes. The queen-retreat variation is analysis; the principal line was played in the game. No mate in one or two solver moves found; the searches are bounded, not an exhaustive proof.
